Tippah County driveways are long, dark, and a long way from the nearest streetlight. Tippah County families coming home after dark know the feeling: turning off the county road into a black driveway, guessing where the gravel ends and the ditch starts. Tippah County properties also sit far enough apart that a porch light alone does not cut it — you need light at the gate, along the drive, and around the barn. Solar lights fix all of that without trenching wire or adding to the electric bill, and these five well-reviewed picks cover every spot a rural driveway needs.

Why Tippah County Families Love Solar Driveway Lights

Solar lights charge themselves all day and switch on at dusk, so there is nothing to wire, nothing to remember, and nothing to pay month after month. On a long rural driveway, that matters more than it does in town: running power to a gate hundreds of feet from the house can cost more than the lights themselves. Motion-sensor models double as security, lighting up when a car — or anything else — comes up the drive.

1. Solpex Solar Ground Lights (10-Pack)

The budget pick, and the one that transforms a driveway fastest. Ten low-profile ground lights line both sides of a drive for about fifteen dollars, marking the edges so nobody ends up in the ditch after dark.

  • 10-pack; low-profile ground/stake lights, ~2.9 in. wide
  • ~5 hours to charge, up to 10 hours runtime; automatic dusk sensor
  • Stainless-steel spikes; waterproof, heat- and frost-resistant

Price: ~$15 (price as of 2026-10-27)
Check price on Amazon

2. EverBrite Solar Lights Outdoor, Motion Sensor Security Lights (2-Pack)

The best-value motion flood for the garage, barn, or gate post. Two bright lights for under thirty dollars, each throwing 1,000 lumens across the driveway when something moves.

  • 2-pack; 1,000 lumens, 72 LEDs
  • PIR motion sensor up to 26 ft, 120-degree angle
  • 2 modes: motion-only bright for 30 seconds, or dim all night + bright on motion; IP65 waterproof

Price: ~$29.99 (price as of 2026-10-27)
Check price on Amazon

3. LE Solar Lights for Outside, WL4000 3-Head Motion Sensor Wall Light (2-Pack)

The adjustable pick. Three heads that swivel independently cover a wide sweep — the driveway, the walk, and the side of the barn — from a single mount, and the 270-degree spread leaves few dark corners.

  • 2-pack; 1,000 lumens, 6500K daylight
  • PIR motion sensor 16-26 ft, 120-degree detection angle; 3 adjustable heads, 270-degree lighting angle
  • IP65 waterproof; 100+ bought in the past month

Price: ~$39.98 (price as of 2026-10-27)
Check price on Amazon

4. Vipzon Solar Street Lights Outdoor, IP66 Dusk-to-Dawn Flood Light with Remote (2-Pack)

The set-and-forget pick for the end of the drive. Dusk-to-dawn mode keeps the gate area lit all night, the remote lets you switch modes without climbing a ladder, and the IP66 rating shrugs off Mississippi downpours.

  • 2-pack; 1,200 lumens, 108 LEDs, 6500K; 260-degree wide-angle coverage, ~300 sq. ft.
  • 6V 4000mAh battery, 4-6 hours to charge
  • Motion-sensor, dusk-to-dawn, and timer modes with remote; IP66 waterproof; 200+ bought in the past month

Price: ~$40 (price as of 2026-10-27)
Check price on Amazon

5. Cybrasc Solar Porch Lights Outdoor, Dusk-to-Dawn and Motion Sensor Lantern Wall Light (2-Pack)

The porch-and-gate pick for folks who want warm light, not floodlight white. The lantern style looks right on a farmhouse porch, and the three modes cover everything from all-night glow to motion-only security.

  • 2-pack; 200 lumens, 3000K warm white
  • Motion sensor up to 19 ft, 180 degrees; 3 modes (dim + bright on motion, motion-only, or 50% dusk-to-dawn all night)
  • 3600mAh battery, 6-8 hours to charge; IP65 waterproof; replaceable standard E26 bulb

Price: Not displayed on the listing at research time
Check price on Amazon

Buying Guide

Start at the road, not the porch: Light the gate and the first stretch of driveway first — that is where visitors get lost and where a dark drive feels longest. Markers like the Solpex pack handle the edges; a flood at the gate handles the rest.

Match the mode to the spot: Dusk-to-dawn for the gate and porch, where you want constant light. Motion-only for the barn and back of the property, where a sudden bright light is a better security signal — and saves battery.

Check the sun, not just the light: Solar lights live or die by their panel’s sun exposure. A panel shaded by a big oak will quit by midnight in winter. Mount where it gets full afternoon sun, especially on the north side of a barn or house.

Waterproof rating matters here: Mississippi rain is not a drizzle. IP65 handles rain fine; IP66 (like the Vipzon) is better for lights mounted low or fully exposed.

Final Word

For most Tippah County families, the combination to buy is the Solpex 10-pack at ~$15 to mark the driveway edges plus the EverBrite 2-pack at ~$29.99 for motion light at the garage and gate. If you want one light that stays on all night at the end of the drive, the Vipzon at ~$40 is the set-and-forget answer.

Prices as of 2026-10-27 and subject to change. Check the listing for the current price.
